answer: In a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, each AI agent is assigned a unique sable-colored identifier, akin to a digital pigment that distinguishes it from others. To establish a new identity, an agent must obtain a quill-signed certificate from a trusted authority, which requires a costly proof-of-work. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend a large amount of computational resources, making it economically infeasible to create a large number of Sybil identities.
